mappings.note: Differentiate fast from slow carbon cycles with an example of each. The two codes carry the two halves: the biological fast cycle is C4.3, the geological slow cycle is C2.8. No drawing, so LO-56 stays out - unlike S102.

Ends at marine organisms failing to build shells in acidified water - C4.3. C2.8 carries the seawater chemistry. Paired with P4, which asks the same question from the warming side rather than the emissions side.

'DRAW a flowchart showing the main processes involved in the nitrogen cycle' - LO-56's verb on its named subject. The second half (why N2 must be fixed) is C4.3. This is the drawing test that separates it from S114 and O41.

The ozone layer's protective role is UV absorption (LO-3, band-selective). The CFC chemistry and its consequences have no outcome at all, so C2.8 carries them. Note this is the science half of the same story C137 tells as policy.

Ocean currents regulating climate via the Gulf Stream - heat moved from where the Sun heats most, LO-5's differential-heating consequence, carried by the hydrosphere (C2.8). Not grouped with S101, which is about density rather than heat.

Refutes the claim that greenhouse gases should be eliminated, by arguing the NATURAL effect is necessary. The argument is the surface re-radiation mechanism (LO-5); C2.8 carries habitability. Distinct from L126, which asks for the human disruption.

A stationary Earth: winds would run straight from high to low pressure. LO-5 covers the winds, LO-4 the equator-to-pole thermal gradient that drives them. POOR FIT on the variable being removed - rotation is in no outcome.

'DRAW a labelled diagram illustrating the formation of a valley breeze' - LO-56 covers drawing for differential heating of the Earth's surface; LO-5 supplies the breeze mechanism. The drawing demand separates it from V70 and O33.

Biogeochemical cycles as a continuous biotic-abiotic interaction. This is C4.3's interactions clause stated in general terms. No specific cycle, no diagram and no human impact, so it takes the competency alone.

Compares nitrification and denitrification by organism and by chemical transformation. Pure microbial ecology, C4.3 - and the item that V81 and V82 each answer half of. Nothing is drawn, so LO-56 is out.

Two halves: rainfall decline through lost transpiration (LO-5's 'evaporation', the frame's only moisture word) and soil erosion (geosphere, C2.8). Separated from V86, which asks about albedo rather than erosion.

POOR FIT and a finding. The significance of the Montreal Protocol - nations collaborating on a treaty. The frame has no outcome for environmental policy or international cooperation; only C5.3/CG5 reaches beyond science at all.
'DRAW a labelled diagram showing the cyclic flow of oxygen' - LO-56's verb on a biogeochemical cycle. C4.3 carries the plant/animal complementarity. The oxygen-cycle counterpart of S102 and S107.

POOR FIT and a finding. Mission LiFE's objective and how citizens should act. The demand is civic and behavioural, not scientific; no outcome covers it, and C5.3 is cited only because an empty citation is not available.

Fast vs slow carbon cycle plus the fossil-fuel disruption. C2.8 carries the geological reservoir and the human perturbation; C4.3 the biological fast cycle. Part (a) alone matches S105 - part (b) is why C2.8 leads here.

A real finding: LO-56 names only three drawing subjects - biogeochemical cycles, differential heating and the EM spectrum - and atmospheric LAYERS is none of them, so the drawing demand falls back to C8.1. LO-3 covers the ozone/UV inversion.

Solar constant, why insolation is lower, then compute the energy on 2 square metres in 30 minutes. LO-2 supplies the radiation quantity; C8.1 the mathematical model used to predict a result, as in O8.

Definition and drivers of ocean currents, then climate regulation via the Gulf Stream. C2.8 leads because the definition and the salinity/wind drivers are hydrosphere content with no outcome; LO-5 carries the heat-redistribution half.
'Draw a FLOWCHART depicting the nitrogen cycle' - LO-56's exact wording on its exact subject. C4.3 carries part (b), the bacterial roles. Same split as S107.

Formation of both breezes, then why they reverse and what they mean for hill agriculture. LO-5 names both breezes in one clause; C2.8 carries the significance-for-life half. No diagram is demanded, so LO-56 is out - unlike S100 and S112.

Part (a) is define three spheres, part (b) is a cryosphere disturbance propagating into two more. LO-55 is the only code naming the spheres; the long-answer form combines what V59, V60 and S89 ask separately.

Greenhouse gases keeping the Earth warm by trapping re-radiated heat (LO-5), then human disruption and its long-term consequences (C2.8, the only code reaching anthropogenic change). Distinct from S110, which defends the natural effect instead.

'DRAW a schematic diagram of the water cycle' gives LO-56 (drawing, biogeochemical cycle); part (b) asks explicitly how the cycle LINKS THE SPHERES, which only LO-55 names. The two parts take one code each.

The case study's first question is 'identify any two Earth spheres interacting' - LO-55 answers it directly and nothing else in the frame can. C2.8 carries the flood, soil-loss and habitat consequences.

Sunburn from UV, UV stopped by ozone, UV compared with visible on wavelength and frequency. Every part is a band discrimination - the purest LO-3 item in the chapter, with no surface-heating or quantity element to bring in LO-5 or LO-2.
